subject: gunblade
pitch:
Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.

spec.name: Gunblade
spec.description: A Final Fantasy gunblade: a long single-edged silver sword with a revolver built into its hilt, a barrel along the spine, a cylinder at the root, a trigger, a hammer and a lion pendant. It stands upright with its point on the floor.
spec.layout: Static prop, no joints. It stands vertically, tip down, with the tip at y=0 (sinking at most 0.02). The blade faces +Z: the sharpened single edge runs along z=+0.075 and the flat spine at z=-0.05, with blade faces toward ±X. The blade is 0.9 m long, 0.12 m wide in z and 0.03 m thick in x, with a swept, slightly forward-curved point. The revolver barrel lies on the back of the spine (center z=-0.075, radius 0.03) and runs from a muzzle at y=0.34 up to the cylinder, so the blade and barrel point the same way like a bayonet. The revolver cylinder (axis along Y, center y=0.97, radius 0.055) sits on the spine side at the blade root, above a compact revolver frame (y 0.88-1.06). Above that is a winged gold guard (y 1.06-1.12, x +-0.16). A trigger guard loop with a trigger projects toward +Z (to z~0.2) at y 1.06-1.2. A hammer curves out the back (-Z, to z~-0.2) at y 1.1-1.2. The straight leather-wrapped grip runs y 1.12-1.36. A lion-motif pommel sits at y 1.36-1.47, with a short chain and a Griever-style lion pendant hanging at x=+0.09. Style is Final Fantasy VIII: polished silver steel with pale cyan bevels and engraved panels, black gunmetal, gold trim and filigree, dark brown leather wrap, and small glowing blue energy inlays in the fuller and cylinder. Shapes are chunky and bold, built from primitives with faceted low-poly edges. Detail comes from small parts seated on the surfaces: rivets, bands, engravings, flutes, chambers, notches and gems. Every part uses only the shared palette. The silhouette is asymmetric and dramatic: a heavy hilt-and-gun mass on top and a long elegant blade below.

parts.builds: The sword blade from the point at y=0 up to the root at y=0.9. It is a flat extruded single-edged silhouette (edge on +Z, spine on -Z) with a swept point and a slightly forward-curved belly. A bright bladeEdge bevel strip runs along the edge side. A bladeShade lower bevel and a darker fuller groove (fuller) run down the centre of each face, with a thin glowBlue inlay line inside the fuller on both faces. A spine band of bladeShade has small stepped notches along the back. The ricasso near the root has two engraved panels (engrave) with a small lion-head emblem and filigree lines on each face, plus gold collar rings (gold, goldDark) at the root. Several tiny rivets (screw) sit along the ricasso. Both faces are decorated alike.
parts.attaches: The point is at mount bladeTip. The root at bladeRoot passes into the revolver frame. The spine at z=-0.05 touches the barrel along spineLineZ.

parts.builds: The gun mass on the blade's back. The barrel is an octagonal gunMetal tube (center z=-0.075, radius 0.03) from the muzzle at y=0.34 to the cylinder. It has a gunDark bore opening at the muzzle with a gold muzzle ring, a top rib, a small front sight, clamp bands (gold and gunLight) joining it to the blade spine, and glowBlue energy slits along its sides. The cylinder (center y=0.97, radius 0.055, y 0.9-1.05) is a faceted drum with six fluted chambers (gunDark holes ringed gold) and glowBlue core rings. Gold rims cap its top and bottom. A bolt notch (gunLight) and a small ruby gem seat on it. The revolver frame (y 0.88-1.06, x +-0.045, z -0.14 to 0.09) has gunMetal side plates, gold trim lines, screws (screw), an ejector rod and a gunDark recess for the blade root. Everything is built from small primitives with a bold chunky look.
parts.attaches: The barrel rests on the blade spine along spineLineZ and barrelAxis. The cylinder is centred at cylinderCenter, and the frame ends at frameTop where the hilt guard starts. The blade root enters the frame at bladeRoot.

parts.builds: Winged gold guard at guardCenter (y 1.06-1.12, x +-0.16): swept-up wing blades with goldDark undersides, a central gunMetal boss, ruby or glowBlue studs at the wing tips, and filigree ridges. A trigger guard loop projects toward +Z from the frame (to z~0.2, y 1.06-1.2) in gold with gunDark trim, with a curved trigger (gunLight) inside it at triggerPivot. A hammer at hammerPivot curves back toward -Z (to z~-0.2) in gunMetal, with a knurled gunLight spur and a pivot screw. The straight grip (y 1.12-1.36) is a leather-wrapped faceted tube with diagonal leatherDark wrap bands, gold ferrules at the top and bottom, and small gold rivets, with a gunDark core visible at the ferrules.
parts.attaches: Sits on the revolver frame at frameTop. The grip axis runs through gripCenter from y=1.12 to y=1.36, where the pommel part starts at pommelBase. The trigger and hammer pivots are the mounts triggerPivot and hammerPivot.

parts.builds: The lion-motif pommel at pommelBase (y 1.36-1.47). It is a gold faceted cap with a goldDark collar, a lionSilver lion-head emblem seated on the front and back (mane spikes, eyes, snout), and a glowBlue gem crowning the top. Hanging from charmAnchor at x=+0.05 to 0.09: a ring, a short chain of small gold links, and a Griever-style lionSilver lion-head pendant with a mane of small spikes, black eyes and a small ruby accent, hanging down to about y=1.22, clear of the grip. A tiny gold clasp joins ring and chain. All made from small primitives.
parts.attaches: Starts at the top of the grip at pommelBase (y=1.36). The chain hangs from the pommel's side at charmAnchor.

calls.reasoning:
I'm envisioning a gunblade design—a large sword with a revolver mechanism built into the hilt, complete with trigger, cylinder, and barrel running along the blade's spine. Since props and scenery can just be plain objects without joints, I'll keep the model static rather than risk adding moving parts for the trigger or cylinder.

Now I'm working out the orientation and dimensions: the weapon stands upright with the blade tip touching the floor at y=0, grip at top, edge facing forward along +Z and spine facing -Z. I'm sketching the proportions—roughly 1.5m total height with a 0.95m blade—and figuring out where the barrel attaches along the back of the blade near the hilt.

I'm placing the revolver frame and cylinder at the top of the blade near the guard, with the cylinder axis running parallel to the blade (along Y) like Squall's gunblade, then planning the grip above it and the blade's engraved details like the fuller and lion emblem below.

Now I'm breaking the design into distinct parts: the blade with its sharpened edge and tip, the gun barrel and cylinder running along the spine with flutes and chambers, and the hilt/frame section containing the trigger guard, grip, pommel, and lion pendant ornament — likely settling on four main components total.

I'm also considering whether the blade's tip should slightly sink into the floor for a grounded stand, deciding a tiny sink is fine but nothing extra like a stand is needed, and starting to work out proportional widths for the guard and other elements.

Now I'm laying out precise geometry coordinates for the sword: blade length, z-axis placement for the edge versus spine to give it an asymmetrical single-edge shape like Squall's gunblade, with the tip curving toward the front edge.

I'm resizing the cylinder to 0.055 radius so it protrudes slightly beyond the frame sides for a realistic revolver look, then aligning the barrel center to overlap with the cylinder and spine at z=-0.075, keeping the cylinder spanning y 0.9–1.05 before positioning the crossguard above it.

Now I'm shaping the guard as wing-like extensions flanking the frame at y~1.1, with the grip running straight vertical from 1.12–1.38, and placing a trigger loop on the front z-side between y 0.96–1.12 to keep the gunblade silhouette close to Squall's design.

Let me dangle the lion pendant charm from the pommel outside the grip radius, keeping it clear of the hilt geometry. With total height settled at 1.47 and overall bounding size defined, I'm starting to lay out the actual part boxes, beginning with the blade's bounding coordinates.

For the blade I need bevel strips, fuller groove, spine notches, engraving, and the etched lion emblem, going for that Final Fantasy look with silver blade, cyan highlights, and gold trim within a 200-part budget. Next I'm boxing out the gun component—barrel, cylinder, frame—including muzzle, bands, sights, chambers, flutes, and screws, then moving into the hilt box covering frame top, guard, trigger assembly, hammer, and wrapped grip.

I'm working through overlap issues between the gun frame and hilt region around y=1.04-1.06, deciding the gun owns the barrel and cylinder up through the lower frame housing while the hilt takes over with the guard starting at y=1.06, then placing the hammer behind at y=1.12-1.2 and positioning the trigger guard just below.

Now I'm laying out part 4 with the pommel and hanging charms: a dangling lanyard from the pommel down to around y=1.2, the grip top ending near y=1.36, then the pommel body and cap extending up to about 1.47. I'm also deciding what decorative elements to include with the Griever-style pendant — thinking through a lion emblem, chain, pendant, glow gem, and ring, while skipping extra feather details.

Still working out the coordinate mounts for each part — tip, blade root, spine line, barrel axis, muzzle, cylinder center, frame top, grip base, trigger pivot, hammer pivot, and pommel base — and setting a small budget of 150 for the charm details, bringing the total build budget to 750.

I'm also defining the guard wings' position between the hilt and blade, then laying out the full color palette: steel and edge tones for the blade, gunmetal and gold for the hardware, leather browns for the grip, and glowing blue accents for the charm.

I'm planning the buildPommelCharm function without joints, using simple geometric parts placed at specific positions, keeping the part count manageable around 100. I'll structure it to accept the shared context object and position the pommel geometry near the top of the model.

Laying out the pommel with a faceted collar, frustum-shaped main body, gemstone crown with glowing core, and gold prongs around the gem, plus a lion emblem on the front and back faces... Writing part geometry...

Building the lion head helper...

Still designing the lion head...

Now I'm working out the pendant scale: picking s=0.05 for the head radius, positioning the center around y=1.26 so the mane spikes extend down to roughly y=1.2075, keeping the whole piece hanging just below y=1.22.

I'm working out the attachment point on the pommel for a small gold lug/eyelet, then running a short chain down to the pendant's top edge, with a tiny torus ring linking the chain to the lug.

Adjusting the ring eyelet positioning...

Working out the tilt angle via atan2, then planning to alternate link orientations by combining quaternion rotations for a realistic chain twist. I'm also placing a small bail ring at the top of the pendant to connect it to the last chain link, aligning its position just above the final link's center.

Now I'm adding a small ruby octahedron accent on the pendant's forehead, computing where it should sit on the face sphere's surface given the scaled z-extent and eye offsets so it reads as embedded rather than floating.

Checking the lower frustum radius near y=1.382 where the mane spikes slightly exceed the surface, which actually reads fine as medallion relief. I'll embed a dark gold backing disc slightly recessed into the surface so the emblem plate sits flush with a touch of protrusion at the lower edge.

Now I'm considering pommel decoration: adding faceted grooves, a rim band, and small stud details near the top shoulder using simple cylinder and cone shapes, keeping to just the gold and dark gold palette, plus a topmost dark gold ring near y=1.437.

Working through the gem placement for the pommel top, I need to size the octahedron gem and its glowing core so the tip stays within the 1.36–1.47 height spec, adjusting the center and scale until the top lands right at 1.470, then laying out the seat frustum beneath it.

Now I'm adding four small gold prong cones around the gem for a classic setting look, applying a glow effect imported from the kit onto the flat-colored gem material, and sketching the goldDark collar ring below the grip transition.

Then I'm checking the geometry of a side lug and eyelet attachment near the pommel, confirming the lug box and ring tube dimensions overlap correctly so the hook sits properly in the XY plane without clipping.

For the pendant, I'm planning a double layer of mane spikes—12 main plus 12 shorter offset ones behind—then tallying up total part counts across pommel, emblems, pendant, and chain to stay under roughly 150 parts, landing around 110.

Still writing lion head geometry...

I'll use bladeEdge for highlights since face and spikes in lionSilver feel too flat together—maybe face stays lionSilver with a brighter bladeEdge snout, dark engraved brow ridges, and black eyes/nose/mouth. I was thinking about small cone ears but they'd clash with the mane spikes, so I'll skip them and consider cheeks instead.

Skipping ears, I'll add tilted engraved brow boxes above the eyes and tiny bladeEdge fang cones pointing down below the snout. I need to double check the z-rotation signs stay symmetric under the facial mirroring, then place a small ruby octahedron on the forehead, working out its surface height so it sits flush against the curved head.

Now I'm planning a helper function that wraps the part placement call, handling position, rotation, and scale—scaling geometry directly before passing it in to avoid ambiguity, using degree-based rotation arrays, and setting cylinders to rotate 90° on the x-axis so their axis runs along z for plate-like shapes. Writing cylinder helper...

Placing the gold band position and adjusting the emblem plate so it sits slightly in front without clipping, then working out stud placement at diagonal angles around the band to avoid overlapping the lug.

I'll add small goldDark diamond shapes at the diagonal angles on the lower body, avoiding collisions with the emblem spikes, alongside the gold studs already placed at those same diagonals, computing their positions with sine/cosine around the circle.

Now I'm working out the chain links as alternating torus shapes (one in the XY plane, rotated 90° for the next to sit in ZY), scaled to be elongated, plus a bail torus connecting to the pendant and a small gold cylinder as a clasp, with link centers interpolated between the ring base and the pendant attachment point.

I need to figure out how to type the Ctx parameter for buildBlade without importing anything unknown—I'll just define a loose local type alias to be safe in case it shadows a global declaration.

Now I'm sketching out the blade's geometry: extruding the outline along x with thickness centred, plotting outline points in the (z,y) plane from tip through the belly curve up to the root at y=0.93, with the spine curving back to a sharp tip. I'm setting thickness to 0.03 and marking the tip point precisely at the floor, then starting to think through the surface details at x = ±0.01.

Defining edge bevel geometry...

Still working out the z-band layout...

Layering the fuller and glow overlays with slightly offset positions, considering using a glow kit function to create the raised painted look rather than an actual groove, then planning a spine band shading strip spanning both faces near the top.

Still placing notch geometry...

For the ricasso area, I'm planning two engraved panels in the y 0.775-0.895 band — an upper one for the lion-head emblem and a lower one for filigree lines, each as a chamfered rectangle with thin engraved color.

For the lion emblem itself, I'm sketching it from a hexagonal outline in lionSilver with mane spikes, black eyes, and a snout, using a helper function to position extruded outlines onto either face symmetrically via an offset coordinate frame.

Now I'm detailing the mane as a star-shaped polygon alternating between two radii in gold, with the face as a smaller octagon in lionSilver, plus small black eye boxes and a gold/black triangular nose. I'm also planning thin gold filigree strips as sinusoidal curls for the lower panel decoration.

Adding rivet details...

Still working out collar ring placements...

Placing the upper lion panel between y 0.775–0.84 centered around z 0.014, sized to fit the mane within the panel height, with a filigree panel below it from y 0.715–0.765. I'm adjusting the panel z-depths slightly so the edge bevels overlap cleanly without gaps, keeping the fuller extending to about y 0.70-0.76 and the lion centered at z 0.006.

Now I'm adding eight rivets per face positioned at the corners of both panels, plus a shaded false-edge bevel strip near the tip along the spine side to suggest a secondary edge detail using a small polygon shape.

Still computing overlay strip coordinates...

Checking the edge bevel polygon coordinates against the silhouette to confirm no intersections at the tip and along the upper blade, then moving to verify the lower bevel shade strip placement.

Still working out blade geometry coordinates...

Still working out layer offsets...

Rivets sit half-sunk into the panel surface near the top edge. I'm also considering small stepped notch details on the spine and faces, and thinking about whether the cutting edge needs an actual sharpened bevel rather than just a flat silhouette—possibly a thin rod swept along the edge polyline to suggest a true blade edge.

Writing edge polygon coordinates...

I realize the strip would be coplanar with the body edge and z-fight, so I'm nudging the strip's outer edge slightly beyond the body (by 0.0006) to make it protrude just enough to render cleanly, adjusting the tip and spine points accordingly before moving to the blade body extrusion with a bevel.

Still defining silhouette points...

I'm setting up the extrusion along the x-axis with a small bevel, then adding ricasso and gunmetal barrel details near the spine. For the fuller, I'm considering thin highlight and shade strips along its edges to give it an engraved, glowing look.

Now I'm adding small dash-like diamond engravings spaced along the flat steel between the spine band and fuller, built with a helper function, then double-checking the overall part count stays well under budget before moving on to the spine band geometry.

I'm placing the spine band box carefully, adjusting its centering and thickness slightly to avoid z-fighting where it would otherwise sit exactly coplanar with the body's spine face.

Now I'm working out the notch pattern along the spine band — spacing them every 0.03 in y for roughly two dozen notches, alternating depths, and checking whether they'd actually be visible given how the barrel shape occludes part of the spine's z-range at those x positions.

Settling on a 0.038 notch width so it barely protrudes past the band. Now I'm designing the lion emblem itself: a 12-point gold star mane, a silver octagon face, a darker snout shape, small black square eyes, and a triangular nose, all positioned relative to the center point.

Layering these from mane to face to snout with slight lift offsets, pulling colors from the palette, and adding engraved detail lines for the mouth. Checking that the mirrored face (s=-1) still reads correctly since the lion is symmetric, then setting up the star outline points and starting the chamfered rectangle panel outline.

Defining more panel coordinates...

Still writing filigree sweep...

Defining the fuller outline points and glow geometry, then adding left and right rim rectangles with slight lifts for depth.

Now I'm writing a helper function to extrude rectangular rim shapes along the blade, then setting up the layering function that computes thickness and offsets each part centered around the blade axis. I'm also adding small sphere-geometry rivets positioned along the hilt.

Writing edge strip outline...

I'm writing the buildHilt function signature using the provided Ctx type without declaring my own, then assembling the parts statically with b.part calls since there are no joints involved.

Now I'm planning the guard geometry in model space: a central gunMetal octagonal boss around y=1.09 with thin gold rings, flanked by swept wing shapes extruded from an outline profile.

I'm positioning the wing outline relative to the attachment point, tapering its thickness, and adding a slightly offset darker gold underside layer beneath the main extrusion to create depth.

Now I'm planning thin filigree ridges along the wing's top surface, trying to work out consistent coordinate points for small rods that trace the wing's curved outline.

Refining the horn shape...

Placing the tip gem, then adding gold collar rings around the boss, a gunmetal octagonal boss cylinder, and small screw details on the wings. For the grip, I'm sizing an octagonal cylinder with gold ferrules capping the top and bottom ends.

Writing spiral wrap geometry...

Sweeping the spiral path into a thin gold tube now, then shifting to shape the trigger guard loop as a curved D-form arcing from the frame bottom forward and up into the z-depth range.

Adjusting tube thickness to an elliptical cross-section so it's wider in x than y, making sure the endpoints tuck into the grip and guard boss regions properly.

Adding more trim pieces... now placing a gold collar block at the frame-loop junction, then sketching the trigger geometry with a curved sweep path from pivot to tip with tapered radius.

Still working out trigger geometry...

I'm routing the trigger curve into the tube's interior and placing pivot screws as small gold cylinders along the x-axis, double-checking the loop tube radius stays within the overall bounds, then moving on to shape the hammer curving back toward the rear of the revolver.

Now I'm building the hammer spur as a tapered catmull sweep rising from the frame pivot up and back, with an ellipse radius narrowing toward the tip, all rendered in gunmetal, plus a small knurled box at the very end for grip detail.

Working out the tilt angle for the spur pad gives about -24°, so I'm computing the axis direction and normal vector needed to place the small ridge boxes correctly along the tilted surface.

Good, θ=24 confirmed with a 24-degree XYZ rotation. Now I'm positioning the pivot screw pieces on the hammer side with gunmetal and gold cylinder details, then placing the hammer base block above the frame.

Adding more layered details...

Placing the secondary wing blade behind the main tip, then figuring out where to put the ruby stud so it sits on an exposed part of the top face without overlapping the secondary blade or the glowBlue accent.

I keep testing ruby placements against the secondary shape's coverage region, trying to shrink or shift the secondary outline so the ruby sits visibly on the main wing's top face instead of getting hidden underneath.

Now I'm working out filigree ridge placements along the main wing top, checking that the ridge rods sit at a z-offset wide enough to peek out from under the secondary's thickness, plus adding dark trim rods along the wing's front and back faces.

Then I'm adding a small glowing blue stud at the main wing tip, positioning a tiny sphere near the tip outline and planning to pull in a glow kit for the emissive effect.

For the central boss, I'm layering a gunmetal cylinder with an inset disc and hex bolt on top, making sure it clears the grip, then wrapping it with gold collar rings above and below to visually secure it against the ferrule.

I'm placing eight small radial screws evenly around the boss using a loop with trigonometric positioning, oriented so each one points outward from the center. Then I'm checking the geometry so the blade, frame, and boss don't overlap -- confirming the boss sits cleanly above the frame without intersecting the blade's root span.

For the boss shape, I decide to stretch it slightly along the z-axis using a scale factor instead of keeping it perfectly circular, giving it more of an elongated ellipse profile, and applying the same scaling to the rings around it. I'm skipping the rear tang detail behind the hammer for now, and giving the leather grip a subtle taper by making it slightly narrower at the top than the bottom.

I'm also adding rivets positioned along the front and back vertices of the octagonal cylinder, working out the geometry so they sit naturally on the ridges where the cylinder's faces meet, and considering rotating the whole shape by 22.5 degrees so a flat face points forward instead of an edge.

Adjusting the ferrule rings with thin gold trim and checking the flush alignment with the pommel base and guard. I'm also sketching out the extrude helper signature for outline-based geometry with directional flipping, and sanity-checking the triangle budget and outline type definitions.

Writing helper functions for geometry...

Adjusting the guard height to gy=1.088, recalculating the dark/gold layer boundaries and ring positions so the tip lands around 1.145-1.183, then nudging the main wing geometry so the top edge aligns near 1.118-1.123.

Still refining the sweep geometry...

Refining the hammer path with four points curving back, placing the pivot pin and smaller base block, then tapering the sweep radius toward the spur pad at the end.

Recalculating with a flatter 40° angle instead, I'm positioning the pad's normal and tangent vectors to place its center just past the spur's end point, offset along the surface normal to account for the pad's length.

For the knurl texture, I'm planning small ridge boxes spaced along the pad's tangent direction, using the same rotation as the pad itself with a dark gun-metal color.

Now I'm moving on to defining the trigger and guard path points.

Now I'm placing the trigger, starting it near the loop top and curving it down toward the grip with a catmull path, keeping its tip radius small. I'm also adding gunmetal trim lines mirrored on either side, a small gold bracket at the loop base, and a tiny gunmetal screw detail.

Then I'm debating whether to add a glow effect near the boss, considering a small glowBlue disc or ring set into a gunmetal inset, but realizing the grip ferrule above it likely covers that area, so I'll skip the extra glow geometry there.

Still defining the box and screw geometry... Now I'm setting up a spiral winding using the builder's spiral helper around the ferrule, with constant radius, several turns and a fine pitch, plus adding small gold rivets near the ferrules for detail.

I'm planning a static buildRevolver function that assembles the geometry from parts without joints, and figuring out how to type the context parameter without importing it directly.

Now I'm working out the actual coordinates—placing the blade, barrel, cylinder, and frame pieces so the cylinder pokes through the frame's window while the side plates and rear strap hold everything together.

Still working out the frame geometry...

Now I'm setting up the barrel as an octagonal cylinder positioned to meet the spine, with the muzzle bore as a dark disc at the end.

I'm adding a top rib box along the barrel's back edge, a small front sight bead at the muzzle in gold, and planning clamp bands at several heights that wrap around to join the barrel to the blade spine.

Positioning gold cheek plates to cover the blade sides over the spine region, alternating with gunlight colors, then adding glowing blue energy slits along the barrel sides.

For the octagonal cross-section, I'm working out that a cylinder with 8 segments naturally places vertices along the ±x and ±z axes rather than flat faces, so I need to rotate it by 22.5 degrees about Y to get flat faces facing those directions, and adjust the radius to 0.0325 so the apothem comes out to the intended 0.03.

Now I'm sizing the slits along the band, placing them at roughly x = ±0.0293 with small box dimensions, and deciding whether to add a glow effect using the existing glow kit utility for shared, cloned emissive materials. I'm also sketching the faceted drum geometry—a cylinder centered near y=0.97 with radius 0.055 and height 0.15, considering a fluted multi-sided look.

Working out drum dimensions and rim colors...

Rather than a full bridge spanning the cylinder top, I'll use an arch approach with front and rear boxes only, placing a thin gunmetal top plate above the gold rim and a small axis cap crowning the cylinder, since the guard above will cover most of it anyway.

For the bottom, I'm adding a gunmetal collar beneath the cylinder connecting it to the frame, positioning the barrel so its end tucks under the cylinder center with enough clearance from the cylinder radius.

For the chambers, I'm planning six fluted grooves around the drum's surface as elongated recessed boxes ringed with gold, spaced evenly to suggest the fluted chamber look of a real revolver.

I'm also noticing a geometry conflict: the cylinder's z-depth overlaps where the blade root sits, so I need to adjust positions so the cylinder doesn't intersect the barrel/blade assembly.

Now I'm placing the flute rotation and orientation, figuring out the box's local axis so it points radially outward and positioning it with sine/cosine of the angle.

Then I'm building the frame's front block: a dark metal core with gunmetal side plates, gold trim lines, screws, ejector rod, and a recess for the blade root, working out the dimensions for the plate chamfers.

Still refining the plate outline...

Placing three screw positions, then adding an engraved recessed panel on the side plate in dark gunmetal with a thin gold border for detail, to be followed by an ejector rod under the barrel.

For the ejector rod, I'm positioning a cylinder running parallel to and offset from the barrel, with a knob at its tip, a small frame housing lug, and a collar at the bottom covering the junction.

I'm also adding a dark gunmetal recess plate beneath the front block to seat the blade root, plus a bottom guard collar along the frame's underside.

I'm widening the dark box slightly beyond the blade so it reads as a visible recess, positioning it just below the frame bottom to protrude a bit. Now I'm working out a rear strap connecting to the back of the cylinder, sizing it to meet the cylinder's surface where it extends backward.

Now thinking about bolt notches and the ruby gem — placing small cylinder stop notches at the six positions between the flutes (at 0°, 60°, 120°, 180°, 240°, 300°), using gunDark slots framed in gunLight near the drum's lower edge to mimic real revolver cylinder stops.

Placing notch bolts at 60/120/240/300 with a decorative bolt notch at 180 alongside the ruby, then adding gold rim bands at the bottom and top of the drum.

Now I'm working out the chamber flute geometry with thin glow rings sandwiched between the gold rims and the flutes, calculating the exact y-coordinates so the ring sits snugly without overlapping the rim or flute edges.

I'm settling on a symmetric drum centered at 0.975, with flutes spanning roughly 0.9325–1.0175 and rings placed at 0.928 and 1.022. For the inner glow, I'm adding a dark recessed flute hole with a glowBlue core and a small glow dot at the top axis cap, then sizing the drum body cylinder to run from 0.9 to 1.05 with collars overlapping just outside that range.

Now I'm working out the 12-sided drum geometry, aligning flutes to face centers rather than vertices by rotating the cylinder 15 degrees so the flat faces line up where I want the flutes positioned.

I'm layering the dark flute box and gold frame at slightly different radial depths so they protrude at different amounts without clipping, then checking that the rings sit close to the flute frame's vertical bounds without overlapping into a z-fight.

I'll embed a thin glow strip within the dark depth, letting it protrude slightly beyond the face for added richness. Now I'm working out the barrel geometry: positioning it from y 0.34 to 0.9, centered at 0.62 with height 0.56, using an octagonal cross-section with radius 0.0325 rotated 22.5°, and setting its z-position so it embeds about 5mm into the spine.

Now I'm designing the muzzle assembly: a gold frustum ring around y 0.34-0.372, a dark bore disc poking slightly below it, a thin inner glow ring around the bore opening, and a second glow band just behind the muzzle ring for added detail.

Adding clamp bands...

Adding energy slits as thin boxes along the barrel sides between the existing bands, spacing them in the gaps around y=.42, .515, and similar intervals to create a segmented glowing effect.

Adding a serrated rib along the barrel back with small notch cuts, then starting on the front sight placement near the top of the rib.

Refining post placement over the rib with a tiny ruby bead on top, and checking that the gold muzzle ring extends slightly beyond the rib base. I'm also setting up the octagonal barrel geometry using an 8-sided cylinder with proper rotation alignment.

Adding more trim details...

I'm checking the geometry fit between the drum and frame plates, confirming the cylinder pokes out past the plate edges since its apothem exceeds the plate width, which seems fine visually.
